title: Weapons · from evidence to inference
description: A presentation path through the saved weapons collection, semantic feature pipeline, neural ensemble, ranked review and finite-population audit.

welcome.title: From a thumbnail to a defensible decision
body: This weapons collection lets us open the computation end to end: image geometry → semantic queries → engineered features → a saved neural model → ranked review and audit.
We will use real saved vectors and weights, then run small interactive experiments to make the mathematics tangible. Every step has a concrete view behind it.

loaded-data.title: Know which weapons dataset is on screen
body: “{{title}}” contains {{records}} records, including {{holdout}} holdout rows and {{previews}} supplied previews. Full numeric calculations can use many more rows than the thumbnail tray shows.
The image collection and paired-video collection answer related but different questions. This tour stays with whichever one is loaded; the counts and capabilities adapt.

detail.title: Two saved evaluation contexts
body: The image collection contains 18,327 rows: 12,833 fit and 5,494 holdout, split by identical image bytes. Its score comes from the saved image-only evaluation refit.

The paired dataset contains 2,875 channel-grouped development-holdout videos. It supports image–text fusion. Its linked thumbnails are current previews and may differ from the historical embedding inputs.

identity.title: Compress the image into useful coordinates
body: The image embedding contains 768 SigLIP coordinates. Cosine matching against 178 image queries produces 178 similarities; pooling these produces 121 engineered features.
The saved model then transforms those features into compact learned codes and a scalar score. The representation rail lets you follow one identity through these spaces.

detail.title: Each transformation changes the geometry
body: A pretrained embedding describes broad visual semantics. A query-similarity vector measures alignment with chosen descriptions. Feature operators express competition and corroboration. A learned code reflects the supervised objective.
These are distinct representations of the same records—not a historical animation of the model learning.
This supplied image overview used cosine distance, 25 neighbors, min_dist 0.15 and seed 42. Labels were not used to fit its coordinates.
Coloring the map by weapon annotations can reveal structure already present in SigLIP. It does not turn the unsupervised map into a classifier.

query-family.title: A weapon can resemble a non-weapon
body: The image bank organizes 178 descriptions into 10 families. Positive descriptions express weapons-related evidence; negative descriptions represent visually competing interpretations.

The initial Explosives family is a useful case study: round or cylindrical objects can share appearance while having very different meanings. Read the actual positive and negative phrases before interpreting a high similarity.

competition.title: Compare “weapon-like” with the competing explanation
body: For the current image and family, a is the strongest active positive description and b is the strongest active negative description.
A strong positive match with an equally strong alternative gives little margin. The feature asks whether the weapon interpretation wins this local semantic competition.

features.title: 178 similarities become 121 image features
body: The saved feature definitions combine family-level extrema, runner-up gaps, margins, gates and smooth pools. Some summarize broader groups of queries.
The 121-dimensional result is the image model’s input. It encodes several ways evidence can be strong, ambiguous or contradicted; it is not simply 121 independent class probabilities.

neural-layer.title: Replay the actual saved network
body: Each member standardizes its feature inputs, computes learned codes, and combines a nonlinear head with a residual linear logit. The supplied graph exposes these operators and parameters.
Three saved ensemble members run separately; their sigmoid probabilities are averaged. The named representation views show member zero. The layer menu can inspect other members too.
Exclude a description and the selected image’s feature vector changes. The frozen evaluation model immediately maps that altered vector to a new score.
This isolates dependence on the chosen evidence. A large score change explains this fitted model’s sensitivity; it does not establish a causal property of the photographed object.

reference.title: A query percentile and a model probability differ
body: In the image collection, the query-margin percentile is an empirical rank transformation of a global positive-minus-negative margin. The image model score is an ensemble sigmoid output.
They can both range from zero to one while conveying different information. The reference view lets you inspect the distribution instead of reading those scales as interchangeable.

grouping.title: A category inventory is not a complete channel
body: The image collection defaults to annotation categories. The paired-video dataset defaults to channel groups, using only the loaded labeled holdout videos.
A high score among the available examples does not imply the inventory is a full census of a channel. Keep that scope attached to any collection summary.
In the image collection, the initial comparison blends a query-margin percentile with the image model. In the paired dataset, it compares image-only and fusion scores.
Changing α reveals which examples depend on the added source. Equal numeric weights do not guarantee equal information or equal reliability.

holdout.title: Protect the meaning of evaluation
body: The image evaluation uses 5,494 byte-grouped holdout rows; the paired data contains 2,875 channel-grouped development-holdout videos.
Use the holdout control and the labeled eligible population when interpreting ranking quality. Every paired video has a thumbnail URL; selecting a point loads its preview on demand.

audit-population.title: Audit the collection you can actually inspect
body: This weapons dataset supplies {{previews}} thumbnail URLs. The mini-audit ranks preview records with a finite score and asks you for new judgments on those images.
All 2,875 paired-video records have thumbnail URLs, so they form the audit population. Review nine images at a time; the intervals describe the ranked population under your chosen question.

audit-question.title: Decide what counts as a weapon
body: The default question is “Select every image containing a weapon.” Before labeling, make the working definition explicit: for example, how you will treat toys, replicas, diagrams and ambiguous objects.
The saved annotations and model scores are evidence from an earlier workflow. Your mini-audit answers are a new set of observations under the question you choose.

reuse.title: From this weapons example to your next experiment
body: We have followed a thumbnail through semantic coordinates, competing descriptions, engineered features, a frozen model, collection summaries, ranking and a finite-population audit.
The tools are generic. This weapons narration is a specialized JSON layer over the default tour; another dataset can bring its own annotations, vectors, model graph and explanation.

feature-atlas.title: From weapon descriptions to a structured feature vector
body: The image query bank supplies 121 features built from 178 text-to-image similarities. The families organize evidence about weapons and competing visual contexts. Each cell refers to an actual exported feature for the selected image.
Open a cell to compare its family’s underlying phrases with the raw operator result. The model receives the whole feature vector, not only the strongest description.

network-flow.title: The saved weapon classifier, one example at a time
body: The image model combines nonlinear feature processing with a linear residual, and averages the supplied ensemble members’ predictions. Follow these branches separately before looking at the combined output.

In the paired collection, image and text representations enter separate learned paths before joining. The same view reads that topology from the exported graph; it is not a different hardcoded diagram.

additions.title: Distinguish saved evidence from a teaching experiment
body: The embeddings, query vectors, engineered features and neural weights come from saved weapons workflow artifacts. The laboratory evaluates these mathematical objects directly.
There are no saved historical training snapshots here. Camera motion and transitions explain representations; they are not an invented record of training.

detail.title: The execution layer and the mathematics
body: In the full auto-classifier workflow, Seamless dispatches configured work to an execution backend and returns artifacts. That layer determines where a computation runs and how results are recovered; it does not define a different cosine, neural layer or posterior.
This laboratory runs supported operations locally in browser workers and WebAssembly. It teaches the artifact-to-calculation contract without pretending that a cloud job is running.

additions.title: Standardize before applying learned weights
body: A feature’s raw numeric scale affects the next layer. The saved normalization subtracts the training reference mean and divides by the saved scale.
Those parameters are part of the fitted function. Refitting them on the displayed holdout would change the function being evaluated.

additions.title: Average probabilities after each member predicts
body: Each ensemble member produces a logit from its head plus residual branch and applies a sigmoid. The ensemble averages the three resulting probabilities.
Averaging logits and then applying one sigmoid would generally produce a different answer. The saved graph preserves the actual order.

additions.title: For paired videos, combine complementary branches
body: The paired graph uses image features plus an image-only probability as one branch input and 229 text-derived features as the other. Its two 8D learned codes concatenate into a 16D joint representation.
The text input came from 1,024D E5 embeddings and 302 text queries. The “Text auxiliary readout” is sigmoid of one member’s text-code coordinate; it is not a standalone text ensemble.
